newsitem.title: SLOVENIA: Slovenia has scope for more coherent policy - D&B.
newsitem.headline: Slovenia has scope for more coherent policy - D&B.

text.p: Slovenia's economy remained buoyant, and an end to recent political uncertainty held out the prospect of a more coherent policy stance, credit rating agency Dun and Bradstreet (D&B) said.
It left its rating for Slovenia unchanged at DB3a for April.

"With a definite solution to three months of political impasse, there is scope for a more coherent policy stance in coming months, especially with regard to the 1997 budget, which has yet to be adopted," the agency said in its latest Risk & Payment review.
Slovenia voted in the new government on February 27, more than three and a half months after the November 10 general election.

"Slovenia's economy remains buoyant and there has been fresh investor interest despite a lack of clarity over central bank regulations forcing international investors to open custody share trading accounts at 14 licensed banks," the agency added.

Since February, when the Bank of Slovenia blocked foreign buying of securities and produced its demand for new accounts, the blue-chip SBI index fell by 18.7 percent, while average daily share trading volume fell to 70 million tolars from a prior 500 million.
Banks said they expected to open the first custodian accounts at the end of April.
The agency said Slovenia's debt burden remained well within its scope of service. -- Marja Novak, Ljubljana newsroom, 386-61-125-8439
